DedicatedIp.description: A dedicated sending IP address owned by the account.

dns_confirmed_at.description: When the PTR hostname was forward-confirmed (PTR → hostname → A record → this IP). The IP carries mail only while this is set.

ptr_hostname.description: Telnyx-managed reverse DNS (PTR) hostname of the IP, in the form `mta-<a-b-c-d>.msgtelnyx.com`. Also used as the EHLO hostname when sending from the IP. Managed by Telnyx and cannot be changed through the API.

quarantine_until.description: Set on release to 30 days after `released_at`. The address is not returned to stock before this time.

region.description: Region label of the allocated IP (for example, `ewr-nj1`).

released_at.description: When the IP was released. Null until release.

status.description: Lifecycle status. `provisioning`: purchased and billed, carries no mail until `start_warmup`. `warming_up`: warm-up ramp in progress. `active`: ramp complete. `suspended`: suspended by Telnyx; carries no mail and is still billed. `released`: returned to Telnyx; carries no mail.

suspension_reason.description: Reason Telnyx recorded when suspending the IP. Null unless `status` is `suspended`.

DedicatedIpBilling.description: Monthly recurring charge (MRC) state for the IP's current allocation.

charged.description: True when `status` is `active`, `stopping`, or `stop_failed`. An IP carries mail only after its charge has been created.

status.description: `not_started`: no charge recorded for the current allocation. `pending`: the charge is queued. `in_progress`: the charge is being created. `active`: the MRC is active. `stopping`: release requested; the MRC stop is being processed. `stopped`: the MRC has stopped. `stop_failed`: the MRC stop failed and the charge remains. `failed`: the charge could not be created.

DedicatedIpCapacityErrorResponse.description: 429 envelope with machine-readable capacity or waitlist meta.

waitlist.description: True when the request was recorded on the waitlist.

DedicatedIpCreateRequest.description: Optional purchase selectors. Each supplied field restricts which stock IP is allocated; neither field is written to the IP. Omit the body or a field to apply no restriction for it. Other fields are ignored.

ip_version.description: Allocate an IP of this address family. Supported value: `ipv4`. Any other value, including `ipv6` or `null`, returns `422`.

region.description: Allocate an IP in this region. Supported value: `ewr-nj1`. Any other value, including an empty string or `null`, returns `422`.

DedicatedIpDeleteRequest.description: Optional release options. The same fields are accepted as query parameters.

drain.description: Set together with `force: true` to release the last IP in a pool. Acknowledges that mail routed to the emptied pool is held until the pool has a sendable IP again.

force.description: Set together with `drain: true` to release the last IP in a pool. Either flag alone has no effect.

reason.description: Free-text reason recorded with the release.

DedicatedIpProvisioning.description: Read-only status of the Telnyx-managed PTR record. No customer action is required to complete it.

checklist.description: Informational progress flags for the Telnyx-managed PTR. They do not gate `start_warmup`; use `dns_status` to check whether the IP can carry mail.

dns_status.description: `dns_confirmed`: the PTR is forward-confirmed and `dns_confirmed_at` is set. `pending_ptr`: the PTR record is not yet in place. `pending_dns`: the PTR record is waiting for forward confirmation. `dns_lost`: a previously confirmed PTR no longer confirms, or the PTR request was abandoned before it ever confirmed (`ptr_request_state` is `abandoned`); the IP carries no mail until DNS is confirmed. `not_applicable`: the IP is released or has no PTR record on file.

ptr_request_pr_url.description: Reference to the Telnyx PTR change request, when one exists. Informational.

ptr_request_state.description: State of the Telnyx PTR change: `pending`, `pr_open`, `merged`, `confirmed`, `failed`, or `abandoned`. Informational.

DedicatedIpUpdateRequest.description: Applies one change per request. `pool_id` takes precedence over warm-up changes: when it is present, the IP moves to that pool (with `weight`, `force`, and `drain`) and other fields are ignored. Otherwise, use `warmup_paused` or `warmup.paused`; a Boolean `warmup_paused` takes precedence. The PTR hostname is managed by Telnyx and cannot be changed: when neither `pool_id` nor a warm-up field is present, a body that includes `ptr_hostname` (including `null`) returns `422` and the IP is unchanged. A body with none of these fields returns the IP unchanged.

drain.description: Set together with `force: true` to move the last IP out of its current pool. Acknowledges that mail routed to the emptied pool is held. Used only with `pool_id`.

force.description: Set together with `drain: true` to move the last IP out of its current pool. Used only with `pool_id`.

pool_id.description: Move the IP to this pool, replacing its current membership. Use the IP's current pool to change only its weight. To take an IP out of a pool, use `DELETE /email/ip_pools/{id}/ips/{ip_id}`.

paused.description: Pause (`true`) or resume (`false`) the warm-up ramp. Used only when `warmup_paused` is not a Boolean.

warmup_paused.description: Pause (`true`) or resume (`false`) the warm-up ramp; equivalent to the `pause_warmup` and `resume_warmup` actions. A Boolean value takes precedence over `warmup.paused`. When a pause field is present and `pool_id` is absent, supplying neither pause field as a Boolean invokes resume.

weight.description: Routing weight in the target pool. Used only with `pool_id`.

DedicatedIpWarmup.description: Warmup ramp state for a dedicated IP.

daily_cap.description: Daily cap of the current ramp stage. Null until the scheduler arms the first stage, and cleared when the ramp completes, automatically or through `complete_warmup`. On an `active` IP this value is informational and can keep an earlier stage cap after a suspension is lifted; it does not limit sending.

paused.description: True while the ramp is paused.

paused_at.description: When the ramp was paused. Null when not paused.

progress.description: Ramp progress (0-100): the share of the 28 send-day schedule completed. Only UTC days on which the IP sent mail count. Set to 100 when the ramp completes, automatically or through `complete_warmup`. On an `active` IP this value is informational and can keep an earlier value after a suspension is lifted.

started_at.description: When `start_warmup` was called. Null before warm-up starts and after release.

today.description: Today's warmup allowance report card (current UTC day). Null outside the warmup window (before start_warmup, after release/suspension). `active` IPs report the ramp-complete allowance, except as described for `cap`.

cap.description: The day's allowance cap. Null when the ramp has not opened yet (day 0: the scheduler has not armed a stage cap) — distinct from a spent day, which reports the cap with remaining 0. `active` IPs report `100000000`, the ramp-complete cap; `complete_warmup` applies it to the current day immediately. A day's allowance created before the IP became `active` can keep its stored `cap` and `remaining` until the next first-attempt send refreshes them.

day.description: The UTC day this snapshot describes (warmup caps reset at UTC midnight).

granted.description: First-attempt sends released from warmup hold so far today. Delivery retries never lease allowance and are not counted.

remaining.description: Headroom left today. A queued send held by the daily cap is explained by remaining == 0; null mirrors cap (ramp not open yet). On an `active` IP whose `cap` is below `100000000`, remaining == 0 is a stored allowance and does not block the next eligible first-attempt send.

BearerAuth.description: Telnyx API key supplied as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. In production, auth may be validated by the API gateway and forwarded via Telnyx auth headers.

Payment.description: Machine Payment Protocol credential used on paid retries, sent as `Authorization: Payment ...`. Obtained by paying a challenge returned in the `WWW-Authenticate` header of a 402 response. This is not a Telnyx API key; initial challenge requests use standard bearer authentication instead.
Payment.name: Authorization

get.description: List the dedicated sending IPs owned by the account, newest first. Narrow the list with `filter[status]`, `filter[pool_id]`, and `filter[region]`; supplied filters combine, so an IP must match every one. An empty value, or a nested or array value such as `filter[status][]=active`, applies no filter, and other `filter[...]` keys are ignored. A value that no IP can match (an unknown status, a `pool_id` that is not a UUID, or a value containing a NUL byte) returns an empty list, not an error.

parameters.description: Return only IPs in this lifecycle status (exact match). Any other value returns an empty list. An empty value applies no filter.

parameters.description: Return only IPs in this pool (exact match on `pool_id`). A value that is not a UUID returns an empty list. An empty value applies no filter.
parameters.name: filter[pool_id]

parameters.description: Return only IPs in this region (exact, case-sensitive match on `region`). An empty value applies no filter.
parameters.name: filter[region]

post.description: Purchase a dedicated sending IP. Requires a verified, enterprise, or legacy account, and an `Idempotency-Key` header: a request without the header returns `400` (code `10015`) and allocates nothing. Telnyx allocates the next available IP from stock. The optional `region` and `ip_version` fields each restrict which stock IP is allocated; they never change the allocated IP's metadata. An omitted field applies no restriction for that field, and omitting the body applies neither restriction. An unsupported selector value returns `422`; a supported value that matches no available IP returns `429` and records the request on the waitlist. Billing: $14/month/IP, charged as a monthly recurring charge (MRC) from purchase. The IP is returned in `provisioning` status with a Telnyx-managed PTR hostname and carries no mail until you call `start_warmup` and add it to a pool that routes mail.

parameters.description: Required. Opaque, unquoted key for safely retrying the same purchase. Keys must contain 1 to 255 letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores. Generate a unique UUID v4 for each purchase and reuse it only when retrying that purchase with the same request. A missing header, or an invalid one —including duplicate, empty, malformed, or overlong values—returns 400 with error code 10015. A request already in progress with the same key returns 409; reusing the key with a different request returns 422. Only successful responses are replayed, for up to 24 hours. Do not include sensitive data in the key.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

delete.description: Release the dedicated IP to Telnyx. The IP stops carrying mail immediately, leaves its pool, and moves to `released`. Telnyx sets `quarantine_until` to 30 days after release. Release requests that the MRC stop asynchronously. Check `billing`: `stopping` means the stop is pending, `stopped` means it completed, and `stop_failed` means the charge remains. If the charge was never created or its creation has not completed, `billing` keeps showing the creation status (`not_started`, `pending`, `in_progress`, or `failed`). Any status except `released` can be released. Releasing the last IP in a pool requires `force=true` and `drain=true`.

post.description: Manually complete the warm-up ramp (`warming_up` to `active`), bypassing the schedule. Use only for an IP already warmed elsewhere. Completion sets `warmup.progress` to `100`, clears `warmup.daily_cap`, and applies the ramp-complete allowance to the current UTC day: `warmup.today.cap` becomes `100000000`, `warmup.today.granted` keeps the sends already released today, and `warmup.today.remaining` becomes `cap` minus `granted`. Once completion applies this allowance, an exhausted stage allowance does not block the next eligible first-attempt send. The response reports these values. On an `active` IP, `warmup.progress` and `warmup.daily_cap` are informational: they can keep earlier values after a suspension is lifted and do not limit sending.
